headline: Microsoft's AI improves weather forecasts up to 6 weeks out
summary: New open-source software uses machine learning to correct biases in existing models, making long-range predictions more accurate and accessible.
details: Microsoft researchers have developed a new, cost-effective method using machine learning to improve weather forecasts up to six weeks in advance. This advancement aims to provide greater certainty for planning by farmers and emergency responders.

The tool, named Probabilistic Bias Correction (PBC), works by identifying and correcting systematic biases in existing weather models, including physics-based and AI-driven ones. This approach addresses the unreliability that typically emerges beyond two weeks of forecasting.

Unlike resource-intensive physics-based models or GPU-dependent generative AI, Microsoft's PBC can reportedly run on standard CPUs. This makes it a more accessible solution for weather agencies with limited resources, potentially democratizing advanced forecasting.

PBC demonstrated significant improvements, enhancing the accuracy of a leading physics-based model for 98% of precipitation and 92% of temperature targets. It also doubled the accuracy of an existing AI forecasting system in study analyses.

This new method is now available as open-source software, encouraging broader adoption and collaboration within the meteorological community. Researchers hope it will enable scientists with fewer resources to contribute to improving weather prediction.

headline_marked: Android uses [[Gemini AI]] to detect scam messages
headline: Android uses Gemini AI to detect scam messages
summary: Google is rolling out new scam protections for Android, including an opt-in feature in Messages that uses Gemini AI to warn you about deceptive texts.
details: Google announced new scam and privacy protections for Android users. An opt-in setting in the Messages app will leverage Gemini AI to analyze sender intent and alert users to potentially deceptive messages.

The Scam Detection feature uses Google's advanced Gemini models to evaluate messages, with analysis performed in a secure, encrypted space called Private AI Compute, ensuring even Google cannot access the data. Gemini Nano will also perform on-device link analysis for safety.

This feature will be available on select devices including Google Pixel 10+, Samsung Galaxy S26 series, and Galaxy Z Fold 8, with broader availability expected later this year through partnerships with manufacturers like Honor, Motorola, and Xiaomi.

Google is also enhancing scam warnings with more context and extra time before users tap on links from unknown numbers. Additionally, Android 15 and newer will receive automatic screen-sharing privacy features, hiding sensitive information like passwords and credit card details by default when sharing screens.

Further protections include call forwarding protection to block apps from secretly enabling it and a verification system for incoming calls from banks, particularly in Brazil, where over three million fake calls have already been blocked since June.
